thread:
IncidentBot: Pager: High ingestion spike detected in apac-embed cluster (service=embeddings), severity=sev2. 95th percentile latency rising, error budget risk. Pager routed to SRE oncall.

maya_k: on it, paging into #incidents. seeing a huge short window spike from ~03:18 UTC. embedding write QPS ~7.2k, baseline ~320.

ow logs: 03:18:12 apac-embed-01 POST /v1/embeddings/batch 429 x1200 origin=unknown-key ip=103.24.88.1
03:18:13 apac-embed-02 POST /v1/embeddings/batch 200 x900 origin=unknown-key ip=103.24.88.2
03:18:14 apac-embed-03 token-refresh 401 x500 origin=proxy-token ip=45.33.22.7

maya_k: majority of traffic looks from a few netblocks and non-customer api_keys. could be credential stuffing + high-volume embedding harvest.

sanjay_r: confirming, I grep'ed the api_key list — ~82% of requests are from rotated anonymous keys with identical user-agent string: "Mozilla/5.0 (embed-crawler)". Looks like orchestrated scraper farm hitting embeddings specifically.

liam_g: customer impact? any paid tenants seeing errors?

emily_cs: AcmeCorp reporting increased 429s for embedding batches from apac region via the support channel. Tiered customers on dedicated pools show some queuing.

maya_k: immediate plan: 1) apply per-key short-term quota and global throttle for unknown keys 2) enable WAF bot signatures for apac region 3) disable batch embeddings endpoint for anonymous/low-tier keys 4) open traffic slice for enterprise customers 5) start customer outreach to affected accounts

ow commands I'm running:
```
# apply per-key rate limit for keys with no org association
rbacctl set-rate-limit --scope=unauth-keys --limit=30/m --burst=60 --duration=15m
# global throttle for APAC embedding cluster
opsctl throttle cluster apac-embed --qps=800 --grace=30s
# enable WAF rule
wafctl enable-rule bot-scrape-v4 --region=apac --action=challenge
```

ow: ops-bot: Executed rbacctl set-rate-limit (ok). opsctl throttle started (qps=800). wafctl rule bot-scrape-v4 enabled (challenge).

ow metrics: ingestion QPS dropped to ~1200 within 2m. errors 429s down by ~60%. latency trending down but still elevated.

ow additional mitigation: disabling the unauthenticated batch endpoint and diverting to single-item endpoints to increase cost for scrapers. command:
```
feature-flag disable embeddings.batch_unauthed --region=apac --until=2026-03-15T06:00:00Z
```

ow: feature-flag toggled (ok)

ow customer comms draft for AcmeCorp (please review):
"Hi AcmeCorp — we observed an elevated rate of embedding requests in APAC affecting batch embeddings. We've applied temporary throttles and a protective WAF rule. Your requests should be recovering; please retry after a short delay. If you still see 429s we'll route you to a dedicated lane. — Emily, Customer Success"

emily_cs: sending now to primary contact, cc'ing solutions.

ow followups:
- @owen_p to take oncall handoff once I step out in 25m
- Sanjay to analyze UA and IP signatures and produce netblock list for firewall blocks
- Liam to coordinate capacity isolate for dedicated customers (if needed)
- Ops to prepare temporary customer-specific rate-limits/routing if recovery stalls

ow sanjay_r: preliminary IP netblocks: 103.24.88.0/22, 45.33.22.0/24, 185.60.90.0/23. I'll push a denylist to edge WAF as a next step.

maya_k: I'm going to add a temporary rule to drop large POST bodies from unauthenticated sources (common for embedding payloads). command:
```
edgectl add-filter --region=apac --match "method==POST && content-length>5000 && auth==none" --action=drop --duration=1h
```

ops-bot: edgectl filter added (id=ef-2468) — dropping ~400 req/s matching filter.

metrics now: QPS ~420, errors stable at baseline. latency returning to normal. AcmeCorp reports improved success in support thread.

ow risk: false positives may affect some legitimate small customers using short-lived keys. mitigation: whitelist known enterprise API keys and dedicated pools before applying broader denylist.

ow handoff: Maya -> Owen. status snapshot for handoff at 03:45 UTC:
- incident started 03:18 UTC, peak ~7.2k embedding QPS, now ~420 after mitigations
- mitigations applied: per-key rate limits, cluster throttle, WAF challenge, feature-flaged batch endpoint for unauth keys, edge filter drop on large POSTs, initial denylist pushed
- impact: some small customers saw 429s; AcmeCorp briefly affected but recovering; dedicated pools OK with some queuing
- next actions: Sanjay to pull full IP list and UA hashes; Owen to monitor APAC embed cluster for 30m and be ready to escalate to capacity isolate; Ops prepare to roll back filters if false positive reports come in

maya_k: handing off to @owen_p — I need to jump to another pager in 20m, leave everything in alerting and runbooks. tagging followups in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

ow owen_p: ack, taking over. I'll watch for any customer impact alerts and keep comms updated. If we need to restore batch endpoint, I'll coordinate with product to do a scoped restore for whitelisted orgs only.

ow emily_cs: AcmeCorp confirmed recovery at 03:52 UTC. sending summary email and thank-you note.

now sanjay_r: I'll produce a short report with UA signatures, IP netblocks, sample payloads, and recommended long-term protections (per-org quotas, token binding, stricter signup throttles). ETA 2 hours.

now incident-bot: Incident marked active -> mitigated. Severity downgraded to sev3. Please file a post-incident review in #postmortems with timeline, root cause hypotheses, and RCA owner.

ow owen_p: copying notes into the incident ticket and will close when metrics are stable for 1 hour. handing off monitoring to next shift.

-- end of thread
